g.title: root-recovery
g.text: Root recovery: a lone revoke runs at once, a bulk action is held
Scenario G: a stolen root credential could stop or sweep every agent of an owner in one session.
Exercised on Monad testnet
Implemented, off or not yet run on testnet
Designed, not built or not deployed
Source: SECURITY.md sections 1, 9; THREAT-MODEL.md scenario G, section 8; libs/recovery

g.title: req
g.text: Owner requests a revoke, rotate, or sweep
From the root wallet, naming one or more agent accounts

g.title: count
g.text: Count distinct agents revoked or swept
By this root wallet in the last 60 minutes,
including the agent now requested

g.title: q
g.text: Hold test
Does the request name two or more agents,
or would the distinct count exceed 3?

g.title: exec
g.text: Execute immediately
One agent, count still 3 or lower
A single revoke never waits

g.title: q->exec
g.text: no

g.title: hold
g.text: Held: nothing executes
The user is notified with the list of agents affected
Recorded per root wallet in the API's recovery log

g.title: q->hold
g.text: yes

g.title: mech
g.text: What a revocation does
Server-held key destroyed first, so no platform process can sign
Owner-signed operation uninstalls the validators and invalidates the nonce
Sponsored outside the per-agent gas budget; result read back from chain

g.title: confirm
g.text: Second confirmation
Restates how many agents are affected

g.title: hold->confirm
g.text: owner confirms

g.title: delay
g.text: 15 minute delay, then execute
A legitimate owner can still retire every agent;
there is no path that skips the hold

g.title: gap
g.text: Paymaster down and no MON in the account
Key is already destroyed on the platform, but the chain still
accepts it until the owner retries; reported as paymaster-unavailable

g.title: chain
g.text: On-chain enforcement of the same rule
Later work (issue 26); today the hold lives in the API

g.title: resid
g.text: Residual risk
An attacker who holds the root credential for longer than 15 minutes
can complete the confirmation; the hold raises cost, it does not remove risk
